data.function: P2 report: Lifecycle read at Digi-Key
data.ruling: The refutation holds for Panasonic. The figure says the Panasonic page for ERJ-6CWDR010V carries no status or could not be read. That is false. The maker's model page answers HTTP 200 and its body gives the model's status as Active. Under the Lifecycle check, the maker's page is the manufacturer status wherever it carries one. So ERJ-6CWDR010V's status is Active from Panasonic, not from the owner's 2026-10-02 Digi-Key substitution. Digi-Key's ProductStatus Active is the distributor figure recorded beside it, and the two sources agree. The part still passes the lifecycle gate, so no part fails because of this ruling. Only the report figure is wrong, and its Panasonic entry must be corrected. P2's scratch shows the only Panasonic page it read was the datasheet PDF AOA0000C313.pdf (17:45:04Z), never the product or model page. The ruling does not cover the other makers in the figure (Isabellenhuette, Vishay, Yageo, Toshiba): those pages were not re-read here. The verifier found no status on them.
data.evidence: Panasonic model page, read 2026-10-02T18:54:38Z: HTTP 200, chrome client, 183,361 bytes, no challenge. Its body has the facet "Product status New (0) Active (1) NRFND (0)" and "Found 1 matches of 4867". The single row listed is "ERJ6CWDR010V ... Current Sensing Resistors Thick Film Type 0.500 2.0 x 1.25 (EIA:0805) 0.0100 0.5 Punched (Paper) Taping ±75". So the one model shown has status Active at the maker.
